authoredPrompt: This figure is a perspective drawing of a toroid with a rectangular cross-section, cut open so the reader faces the flat end of the ring. The gray body carries fine radial hatching across its curved upper surface, and the central hole opens through the middle. Across the top, four horizontal dimension arrows stack in registration with a dashed vertical center line: the longest reaches the outer wall and is labeled R2, the next reaches the inner wall and is labeled R1, a third labeled r ends partway out, and a short one labeled dr marks a narrow increment just beyond it. At the right edge a vertical bracket labeled h gives the height of the rectangular face. Inside that face, at radius r, a thin vertical strip of width dr is filled solid orange and tagged da by a curved leader. A red arrow labeled i curls onto the left end of the ring, and two blue curved arrows sweep along the lower body in the direction of the circulating field. Setting one narrow shaded strip against the full cross-section signals that the flux is built up by integrating such elements outward from R1 to R2, which is what the self-inductance calculation requires.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for radius r: the learner drags the orange da strip from R1 toward R2, the strip moves across the rectangular cross-section while B(r) and dPhi values update, showing why each radial slice contributes a different amount of flux.
- Toggle between single slice and accumulated integral: the learner switches from one highlighted dr strip to the filled region swept from R1 to the current r, revealing how summing dPhi over radius builds the toroid's total flux linkage.

discrepancies: The da strip sits on the left cut end face while in the source it is on the right end face, so the r/dr witness lines and the strip read as slightly disjoint from the dimension arrows
